overview: The Top 'K' Elements pattern is a sorting and filtering design template used to find, track, or sort the $K$ largest, smallest, or most frequent elements in a large dataset. Instead of sorting the entire dataset of size $N$—which takes $O(N \log N)$ time—this pattern maintains a running heap (priority queue) of size $K$. By comparing incoming elements against the root of the heap, we can dynamically evict elements that fall out of the top bounds. This reduces the time complexity to $O(N \log K)$ and requires only $O(K)$ auxiliary space.
recognition_signals: Unsorted Arrays or Streams: The input elements arrive out of order, or are generated dynamically.
Frequency Counting: The problem involves finding elements based on how often they occur.
The "K" Target: The problem explicitly asks for the largest, smallest, closest, or most frequent $K$ elements.
Sub-Sorting Bounds: The expected time complexity is $O(N \log K)$, which is better than standard $O(N \log N)$ sorting.
String Reorganization: Rearranging characters so that duplicate letters are separated by at least $K$ spaces, or scheduling tasks with cooldown gaps.

mental_model.analogy: Imagine a 10-place gaming leaderboard or a VIP concert security queue.
mental_model.description:
Imagine a **10-place gaming leaderboard** or a **VIP concert security queue**.

To maintain the list of the top 10 highest scorers, you do not need to record and sort the scores of all one million players who play the game. You only need a board with 10 slots. The player with the lowest score on the board sits at slot 10. When a new player finishes, you compare their score with slot 10. If the new score is lower, you discard it. If it is higher, you remove slot 10, insert the new player, and let them bubble up to their correct position. The vast majority of scores are discarded instantly.

brute_force_journey.brute_force_description: The brute force approach to finding the top $K$ largest elements is to sort the array in descending order and return the first $K$ elements.
brute_force_journey.inefficiency_observation: Overlapping subsegments perform duplicate evaluations of identical elements.
brute_force_journey.optimization_concept:
```
  Brute Force
  [Sort the entire array of size N to access the top K elements -> O(N log N)]
       ↓
  Observation
  [We only need to track the top K elements, not sort the remaining N - K items]
       ↓
  Optimization
  [Build a Min-Heap of size K; replace the root if a larger element is found]
       ↓
  Final Pattern
  [Logarithmic updates in a bounded priority queue of size K -> O(N log K)]
```

variants.name: **K Closest Points**
variants.description: Max-Heap (Sort by distance; push if `dist < heap.top()`)

variants.name: **Connect Ropes**
variants.description: Min-Heap (Pop two smallest elements, sum them, and push back.)

variants.name: **K Frequent Elements**
variants.description: Min-Heap (Track frequencies in Map; sort heap by frequency.)

variants.name: **K-Distance Apart**
variants.description: Max-Heap (Reorganize string; use cooldown queue to re-add elements.)

variants.name: **Task Scheduler**
variants.description: Max-Heap (Run highest frequency task first; decrement and queue cooldown.)

variants.name: **Frequency Stack**
variants.description: Map + Stack (Store elements in stacks grouped by frequency.)

common_mistakes.description: **Incorrect Heap Type Choice:** Using a Max-Heap instead of a Min-Heap when searching for the *largest* $K$ elements. A Min-Heap keeps the smallest of the top $K$ elements at the root, allowing for an instant $O(1)$ comparison to decide if a new element qualifies.
**Not checking heap bounds:** Pushing elements without checking if the heap size has exceeded $K$, leading to unbounded memory usage.
**Frequency tie-breaking failures:** In frequency stack problems, failing to pop elements in LIFO order when their frequencies are equal.
**Task Scheduler idle counts:** Incorrectly calculating cooldown slots, resulting in off-by-one scheduling durations.

cheat_sheet: To find the largest, use a Min-Heap. To find the smallest, use a Max-Heap.
When organizing strings or scheduling tasks, count frequencies in a hash map first, push counts to a heap, and use a temporary waiting list to respect cooldown limits.
